minutes.headline: Open Space Committee took no action on the 100 Howard Street right of first refusal and will meet jointly with Planning.
minutes.summary: The committee approved the February 28 minutes, heard that the Select Board declined to act on the Pearl Road or Stump Cove parcels, and discussed backing the Shady Point offer of non-motorized lake access. It reviewed the 100 Howard Street Chapter 61 parcel against its checklist but decided to take no action and to meet jointly with the Planning Board before the April 8 Select Board deadline. Residents spoke in favor of the Shady Point offer, and the committee discussed future projects.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee took no action on the right of first refusal for the 100 Howard Street Chapter 61 parcel at this meeting.
The chair will ask members about a joint meeting with the Planning Board at 6 pm on March 25, before Planning's public hearing.
The committee heard the Select Board declined to act on the Pearl Road and Stump Cove parcels, and discussed the Shady Point offer of non-motorized lake access.
Four residents spoke on Shady Point lake access; the comments favored the offer or raised concerns about weeds, motorized boats and unmonitored access.
The committee set April 10 and May 8 meetings and named next projects, including a protocol with Planning for Chapter 61 recommendations.

why_it_matters: Chapter 61 gives the town a short window to match a sale of forest, farm or recreation land, so how quickly boards can agree on a recommendation decides whether open space can be bought before the deadline.
The committee discussed a possible override and having no fund to act on parcels without waiting for town meeting, which bears on whether a land purchase would come to residents for a vote.
watch_next: The joint meeting with the Planning Board proposed for 6 pm on March 25, ahead of the April 8 Select Board deadline on 100 Howard Street.
